docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The idea was to recreate Frostpunk 1 as a first-person RP survival experience where you start as a survivor near the crater, with just the generator and a few basic supply piles—just like the beginning of a classic Frostpunk game.

You’ll gather resources and bring them to the resource depot, stockpiling coal to run the generator at higher power levels. From there, the mayor begins constructing the first essential buildings: tents for housing, a sawmill to turn logs into planks, a medical post to craft supplies and treat frostbite, a hothouse to grow crops, and more.

Every building serves a purpose, and as you contribute to the community, you’ll earn skill points to unlock new abilities and crafting recipes—similar to Frostpunk’s tech tree, but on a personal level. You won’t be able to do everything yourself. Everyone in the community will need to find their own role. One player might become the tailor, crafting insulated coats; another the cook; someone else might train to become the doctor. No one can be a jack of all trades—and that’s by design.

Once you’ve secured the basics to survive the first storm, you’ll start building more advanced structures, and eventually set out on expeditions—to hunt, scavenge, or search for rare resources and ingredients.

And of course, anything is possible. Maybe you don’t like the mayor’s rules. Maybe the community agrees. Maybe you exile him—and become the new mayor yourself.

docs.title: Settlements
docs.text: Members of the governing faction can establish outposts beyond the colony. The settlement guide explains how to found one, supply its depot and build within its boundaries.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: Track personal objectives and shared faction progress in the quest menu. The quest guide explains the tabs, quest states, prerequisites and progress notifications.

docs.title: Heatstamps
docs.text: Heatstamps are the soft currency of the colony. They are rewarded for doing laber work and are generally needed to perform crafting or trade for local things.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: Quests give you objectives to work towards as an individual or together with your faction. Use the quest menu to read objectives, check progress and see what becomes available next.

docs.title: Opening the menu
docs.text: Press J to open Quests. You can change this binding under FROST → Open Quests in the controls settings. Press J again, Escape, or the close button to return to the game.

docs.title: Personal and faction quests
docs.text:
Use the tabs at the top of the menu to switch between:

  • PLAYER — your personal quest lines. Your progress belongs to you.
  • Your faction — shared quest lines for your current faction. Contributions advance the faction's progress rather than your personal progress.

Only your personal tab and your current faction's tab are available during normal play. If you have not joined a faction, you will only see PLAYER. Changing faction updates the available faction tab.

docs.title: Reading quest lines
docs.text:
Each row represents a quest line. Hover over the large icon on the left to read the line's title and description.

Inside the row, each quest has an icon and a name. Hover over a quest icon to see its description, objective, state, progress and any listed reward. You can inspect locked quests too. Scroll the menu when there are more quests than fit on screen.

Lines between quest icons show a connected sequence. Quests without a connecting line can be independent objectives; read their details to check what is required.

docs.title: Quest states
docs.text:
The quest icon and outline use color to indicate its state:

State Appearance Meaning Locked Gray The quest is not available yet. Available White You can work on the objective. In progress Light blue The quest is underway. Completed Pale green The objective has been completed.

Hover over the icon to read the state if you are unsure of its color.

docs.title: Prerequisites and progress
docs.text:
Some quests require another quest to be completed first. Completing that prerequisite unlocks the next quest automatically. Actions performed before the prerequisite is complete do not add progress to the dependent quest, so check that it is available before working on it.

Follow the objective in the quest's popup. Progress updates automatically when a qualifying action is completed; opening or clicking a quest does not complete it.

Personal and faction progress are tracked separately. Progress is saved on the server and restored when you reconnect. Updates appear automatically, so you do not need to reopen the menu to refresh them.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
When a personal quest changes, a notification appears for five seconds with its name and progress. Completing it displays a Quest completed notification. Unlocking a following quest may also produce a notification.

Loading your saved progress when you connect does not produce these notifications. Check the faction tab to follow shared faction progress.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
Buildings can be built by the governing faction. Building menu can be by default opened with N key.

Hover over a building to see its description, resource costs and a short placement diagnostic. Inside an established territory, construction uses only a resource depot in that same territory. Founding a new settlement uses loose resources near your character instead. See Creating a settlement for founding, spacing and resource rules.

Once you select building to build, hologram of selected building will appear. You can rotate the hologram with your mouse wheel. Keep in mind that the hologram cannot be blocked or overlapped by any building, player, or immovable object.

docs.title: Repairing buildings
docs.text:
Snowfall wears down some buildings over time. Look at a building to check its condition. Members of the governing faction can repair these buildings when they are Worn, Damaged, or Badly Damaged.

Hold a hammer, stand close to the building, and use Repair Building. The nearest resource depot in the building's territory must have at least 1 processed wood. Completing the action consumes that wood and restores the building to full health.

docs.title: Coal Mine
docs.text:
The Coal Mine provides infinite source of coal . It needs to powered by the generator. Once the generator is running, machine operators can turn on the the Coal Mine on top of the ladder in the control room.

If the generator is running, coal pile will appear on the back side of the of Coal Mine by the coal pile. This coal pile then needs to be mined.

docs.title: Execution Platform
docs.text: The Execution Platform is used for public exhibitions and executions.

docs.title: Fighting Pit
docs.text: In the Fighting Pit people can settle differneces or bet on boxing matches. This building is not powered by the generator.

docs.title: Gathering Post
docs.text: The Gathering Post provides remote heated shelter outside of the generator's heat range.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text: Access to the resource depot can be unlock via the Resource Depot upgrade. It allows players to put resources into the depot by accessing the wheel barrow.

docs.title: Hunter's hut
docs.text: The Hunter's Hut comes with a workbench that allows players to craft hunting weapons, ammunition and process animal hides into leather.

docs.title: Medical Post
docs.text: The Medical Post offers a place to care for the sick. Its upgrades unlock a resting bed and a medical workbench.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
Upgrade Cost Benefit Common Care 1 Fabric Allows an inhabitant to rest in the bed and recover from common illnesses. Pharmacy 2 Processed Wood, 1 Processed Metal, 2 Fabric, 2 Leather Adds a workbench for preparing medicine, tinctures, and bandages.

These upgrades can be installed independently.

docs.title: Common Care
docs.text:
With Common Care installed, look at the bed and choose Rest to lie down. Your hands must be empty, and only one player can rest at a time. The bed becomes available again when that player stops resting or leaves.

Resting helps cure cholera, influenza, salmonella, and food poisoning. Recovery follows the rate at which the illness would normally progress, while faster recovery from medicine or natural immunity is preserved. Treatment lasts only while resting in the bed.

docs.title: Pharmacy
docs.text: The medical workbench becomes available when Pharmacy is installed. Use it to craft medical supplies; the Medical Post does not provide a workbench before this upgrade.

docs.title: Public House
docs.text: The Public House is a place for the colonists to spend their time off work.

docs.title: Resource Depot
docs.text:
The Resource Depot is the place to store resources.

In order to deposit resources player must walk up to the right spots and use the action to open the deposit window.

Player can then place resources into the invenory of the depot and click the submit button. Once submitted, player receives reward in form of heat stamps.

Resources for building and resource-paying upgrades are taken only from a depot inside the building's territory. Nearby loose resources and depots in another territory cannot supplement the cost. Founding a new settlement uses nearby loose resources instead; see Creating a settlement.

The generator automatically draws coal from the depot at power levels 1–3. Level 0 uses no coal.

The Charcoal Kiln automatically withdraws 1 Raw Wood from its nearest depot and deposits 4 Coal into the same depot every minute while running.

docs.title: Creating a settlement
docs.text: A settlement is an outpost of the colony. You establish one by placing a founding-capable building in unclaimed wilderness. There is no separate settlement marker or approval step.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Be a member of the colony's current governing faction.
  • Empty your hands before opening the building menu.
  • Gather the materials shown for Resourcedepot, the current founding building.
  • Find a suitable location outside the colony and existing settlements.

Your settlement will have a 60-metre radius, centered on the founding building's placement point. Its boundary must be at least 200 metres from every other territory boundary.

Neighbouring territory Minimum distance from your founding point to its centre Colony 430 metres Another settlement 320 metres

Distances are horizontal. Hills and valleys do not change territory membership or spacing.

docs.title: Found your settlement
docs.text:
1. Open the building menu using your Open Building Menu keybind.
  2. Select Resourcedepot in the TECH category. Hover over its entry to see the cost and a short diagnostic.
  3. Put the required resources on the ground within 3 metres of your character. Resources in your inventory or containers do not count for founding. Existing depots cannot pay the founding cost.
  4. Move the hologram to your intended founding point. Keep your character near the loose resources while completing the action.
  5. Read the placement notifications. Move farther away if the candidate overlaps another territory or is too close. A valid founding location shows Creates a new settlement outpost and Territory rules allow placement.
  6. Complete Place Building. A successful placement creates the depot and settlement, consumes the founding materials and displays Settlement founded with its assigned name.

Note: Territory rules allow placement confirms the territory check only. You still need permission, sufficient resources and a valid building position. Slopes, collisions and building-specific requirements can prevent placement.

Previewing or canceling does not claim land. If another player founds a conflicting settlement before your action finishes, your placement is rejected without a resource charge.

docs.title: Build inside your settlement
docs.text:
Stock your resource depot before placing more buildings. Construction inside an established territory uses only a depot within that same territory. Loose materials on the ground and depots outside the settlement cannot supply or supplement the cost.

In the current catalogue, settlements permit:

  • Resource depots.
  • The guard tower.
  • Plain plank variants: 1×1, 1×2, 2×1, 2×2, 3×1 and 3×2.

Angled and pipe plank variants remain colony-only. Most other buildings also remain colony-only. A building being allowed inside a settlement does not mean it can found one: the current founding entry is Resourcedepot.

Membership depends on the building's placement point. That point must lie inside the settlement, including its exact edge; the building's geometry may extend beyond the boundary if ordinary placement checks allow it.

docs.title: Upgrades and upkeep
docs.text:
• Resource-paying upgrades use a depot in the building's territory, regardless of where your character stands. Nearby resources and foreign depots cannot pay for them.
  • Building repairs use one processed wood from the nearest depot in the building's territory.
  • Keep a depot available: without one, resource-paying construction and upgrades cannot proceed, including construction of a replacement depot.
  • Settlement boundaries stay fixed. Adding buildings does not expand or move them.
  • Settlements survive normal server restarts and remain claimed even after every building is removed.
  • Founding grants no personal ownership or special building privilege. Authority follows the colony's current governing faction.

docs.title: Quick troubleshooting
docs.text:
Message or problem What to check Invalid territory This building is not permitted in the area at the checked origin. Settlement required Use an existing settlement; this building cannot found one. Overlapping territory Move the founding point away from the neighbouring territory. Too close to existing territory Allow at least 200 metres between territory boundaries. Missing resources For founding, check loose materials near your character. Inside a settlement, check its depot stock. No permission Confirm that you belong to the current governing faction. Territory allowed, but placement unavailable Check resources, slope, collisions and the building's placement requirements.

Menu diagnostics use your character's position before you choose a hologram location. During placement, territory checks use the hologram's position. Placement notifications appear for six seconds and repeat only when the territory status changes.

docs.title: Related guides
docs.text:

  • Resource Depot
  • Building upgrades
  • Governing faction and voting

docs.title: Tentshack & Bunkhouse
docs.text:
Both Tentshack and Bunkhouse are places to rest and store your personal belongings. There is limited amount of people who can claim said buildings as their home and use personal storage.

In order to get personal storage player must be granted permission from the governing faction. Once permission is granted, player can walk up to the crate in the Tentshack or one of the rooms in the Bunkhouse and claim storage via the action. This provides options to access your storage or if not needed, abandon it.

docs.title: Tentshack Upgrades
docs.text:
Install upgrades to improve your Tentshack.

Upgrade Cost Benefit Requires Storage 3 Processed Wood Unlocks personal storage for up to 10 inhabitants. None Heating 4 Processed Metal Unlocks automatic heating whenever the territory's generator is running. None Insulation 4 Fabric Adds 1 heat level while Heating is installed and powered. None Improved Heating 6 Processed Metal Adds 1 heat level while Heating is powered. Heating

With Heating installed, the Tentshack warms up automatically at any running generator level. It starts at 1 heat level, plus the generator bonus and installed heat upgrades. Insulation can be installed on its own, with its warmth bonus taking effect once Heating is installed and powered. Heating adds zero coal use.

docs.title: Bunkhouse Upgrades
docs.text:
The Bunkhouse uses generator heating and already provides personal storage. It starts at 2 heat levels, plus the generator bonus and installed heat upgrades.

Upgrade Cost Benefit Insulation 4 Fabric Adds 2 heat levels while powered. Improved Heating 6 Processed Metal Adds 1 heat level while powered.

Both upgrades can be installed independently, and their benefits combine while the generator is heating the building.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
Some buildings can be upgraded by the governing faction.

Buildings which can be upgraded will grant a F-action at the building. Upgrades do not come for free but cost resources the same way as building.

Resources for an upgrade are consumed only from a depot in the building's territory, regardless of where your character stands. Nearby loose resources and depots outside that territory cannot pay for it. A resource-paying upgrade cannot proceed without a suitable stocked depot. See Creating a settlement for settlement upkeep rules.

Some upgrades require other upgrades to be installed first.

docs.title: Building upgrade lists
docs.text:
• Tentshack and Bunkhouse: housing, insulation, and improved heating.

  • Medical Post: Common Care and Pharmacy.

  • Generator: three power-level upgrades.

  • Sawmill: Sharp Blade for improved wood yield.

docs.title: Wall Drill
docs.text: The Wall Drill is an infinite source of raw wood . It needs to powered by the generator. Once the generator is running, machine operators can start the Wall Drill.

docs.title: Beacon
docs.text:
The Beacon is powered by the generator. If the generator is not running, player is unable to use this building.

Once the generator is running, player can raise the beacon. Once the beacon is raised to the maximum height, player with forecast skill can predict upcoming weather. The higher the skill, the longer the prediction.

docs.title: Cemetery
docs.text: The Cemetery is can be used by gravediggers to dispose of dead bodies near it. In order to dispose of dead body, gravedigger needs a shovel. This building is not powered by the generator.

docs.title: Cookhouse
docs.text: The Cookhouse is used to prepare and cook meals. Part of the Cookhouse is workbench that is used for crafting complex meals. Meals can be then cooked on a stove inside. This building is not powered by the generator.

docs.title: Generator
docs.text: The Generator powers buildings in its territory, including the Coal Mine and Beacon. The governing faction can switch it on or off and adjust its power level.

docs.title: Power and coal
docs.text:
Level 0 powers buildings and warms shelters without using coal. Higher levels automatically draw coal from the Resource Depot.

Power level Approximate running time per coal Bonus heat for buildings 0 No coal required 0 1 5 minutes +1 2 2 minutes 30 seconds +2 3 1 minute 40 seconds +3

If you try to start the Generator at a coal-consuming level or raise it to one with no fuel available, it stays in its current state. A Generator already running at levels 1–3 shuts down when it runs out of coal. The side gauges show the Generator's heat and the coal available in the depot.

docs.title: Heating
docs.text:
The area around the Generator provides 3 heat levels while it is running at any power level. Generator-heated buildings have their own starting warmth, plus the bonus in the table and any installed heating upgrades. If several generators serve a territory, buildings use the highest level currently running.

Heat builds up after the Generator starts and fades after it shuts down during play. After a server restart, a running Generator and its powered buildings start at their full heat for that power level.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
The Generator's upgrades unlock higher power levels for stronger heating. Install them in order.

Upgrade Cost Requires Power Level 1 1 Steam Core None Power Level 2 1 Steam Core Power Level 1 Power Level 3 1 Steam Core Power Level 2

Installing an upgrade unlocks that power level; use the Generator's controls to raise or lower its operating level. Unlocking all three levels costs 3 Steam Cores in total.

docs.title: Hothouse
docs.text: In the Hothouse players can grow crops and get fresh water. Keep in mind that if the doors are opened or the generator is not running, crops will freeze. It is recommended to fertilize crops to speed up the growing process and provide bigger yield of crops.

docs.title: Kiln
docs.text:
The Charcoal Kiln converts Raw Wood into Coal while the generator in its territory is running.

Close both kiln doors, then use Turn On at the valve. Use Turn Off at the valve to stop production. The doors remain locked and the kiln provides heat while it is running.

Every minute, the kiln automatically withdraws 1 Raw Wood (WoodRaw) from the nearest resource depot and deposits 4 Coal into that same depot. The first conversion happens after one full minute. Raw Wood must be available in the depot before the kiln can start.

The kiln stops if its generator stops or it cannot withdraw Raw Wood for the next conversion. Turn it on again after restoring power or replenishing the depot.

docs.title: Sawmill
docs.text: The Sawmill is used to turn raw wood into processed wood . It needs to powered by the generator. Once the generator is running, machine operators can place log inside the cabin and start processing the wooden log. Once the process starts, wooden log will go through the Sawmill and saw blade will cut it in half. This process also yields sawdust.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
The Sawmill has one upgrade:

Upgrade Cost Benefit Sharp Blade 5 Processed Metal Increases processed wood output from each log.

With Sharp Blade installed, each log produces 4 wooden planks instead of 3. No other upgrade is required.

docs.title: Steelworks
docs.text:
Steelworks is an infinite source of raw metal . Raw metal can be found on the pile near the entrance. Keep in mind that even though this is an infinite source of raw metal, it replenishes over time. Hence why you might not find raw metal at the pile at all times.

This building can also process raw metal into ingots. For this process it needs to powered by the generator. Once the generator is running, machine operators can turn on the the Steelworks. Once the Steelworks are running, player can process the raw metal into an ingot near the mold.

This building also has a workbench for processing ingots and creating processed metal .

docs.title: Workshop
docs.text: The Workshop is the Technical Hub of the colony. Here you can craft various advancements, tools, or clothing.

docs.title: Crafting
docs.text:
There are 2 types of crafting

  • Crafting in hands
  • Crafting in workbenches

docs.title: Crafting in hands
docs.text: It is simple crafting that allows basic day to day stuff such as sharpening tools, refilling canteens or canisters, tearing up old clothes etc.

docs.title: Crafting in workbenches
docs.text:
Some of the buildings provide crafting stations called workbenches. These workbenches allow advanced crafting with multiple crafting ingredients. Usually recipes need to be unlocked with skills and require some amount of heat stamps. Workbenches by default have storage. During crafting, ingredients are taken not only from this storage but also from player's inventory. If workbench does not have any form of storage, igredients are taken only from player's inventory.

Once you select recipe in the crafting menu, you will see ingredients required for crafting. For each of the ingredients you can see on the right side of the / how many pieces or how much percentage (in case of items with percentage) of said ingredient is required. On the left side of the / you can see ingredients available in player's inventory and in the storage of workbench that is being used. Once player gathers all required resources, he is allowed to craft desired item.

If player clicks on recipe with middle mouse button, window with further description of the selected item will appear. This description is classic vanilla DayZ description showing weight, heat insulation or description of said item.

docs.title: Faithkeepers
docs.text:
The Faithkeepers arise as spiritual guardians of the city, embodying the belief that only faith, devotion, and shared belief can preserve humanity against the frozen wasteland. They are the priests, caretakers, and inquisitors of belief, guiding the people not through written law, but through divine purpose. They are often seen wearing robes and symbols of faith, marking them as servants of something greater than the individual.

They move among the population offering prayer, comfort, and direction, striving to keep despair from consuming the fragile community. To the starving, the sick, and the hopeless, they appear as shepherds who promise meaning and hope beyond suffering. Yet to skeptics and dissenters, they are feared as fanatics who demand obedience to doctrine above reason.

Their philosophy is unwavering: without faith, there is no survival. They see doubt as corruption, and heresy as a contagion more dangerous than the frost itself. This conviction drives them to impose strict rituals, public penance, and severe punishment for blasphemy or defiance, measures many citizens consider extreme but spiritually necessary. For the Faithkeepers, justice is not about law or fairness, but about salvation through belief, unity, and unquestioned devotion.

docs.title: Frostlanders
docs.text:
The Pilgrims, also known as Frostlanders, arise as outcasts and zealots of survival, embodying the belief that humanity must abandon cities, laws, and machines to endure the frozen world. They are raiders, hermits, and mystics who have rejected the colony and its technology, choosing instead to live by instinct, hardship, and brutal self-reliance. They are often glimpsed wrapped in frost-scarred garments and ritual markings, their presence marked more by fear than familiarity.

They roam the wasteland beyond the city’s reach, preying on expeditions and striking isolated outposts without warning. To those who venture into the ice, they are whispered of as killers and thieves—figures who rob supplies, sabotage machinery, and leave survivors to freeze if it ensures their own survival. In rare cases, expeditioners have managed to bribe them for safe passage to derelict ruins, or even trade supplies and information under tense, unspoken terms. To the city at large, they remain living proof of what humanity becomes when order collapses.

Their philosophy is ruthless: only the strong deserve to live. They see the generator as a chain, technology as weakness, and community as an illusion that will shatter under true hardship. This belief drives them to destroy what they cannot control and scavenge what they cannot replace, valuing survival above morality. For the Pilgrims, justice does not exist—only endurance, instinct, and the cold judgment of the frost itself.

docs.title: Lawkeepers
docs.text:
The Lawkeepers arise as enforcers of the order, embodying the belief that only strict discipline, absolute loyalty, and uncompromising justice can preserve humanity against the frozen wasteland. They are the guards or watchmen, who try to enforce the law in a city. Usually they can be seen wearing blue colored clothes distinguishing them from regular citizens.

They patrol the streets trying to prevent chaos and crime from swallowing the fragile community. To the starving, the sick, and the hopeless, they may appear as protectors. Yet to dissenters and rebels, they are feared as instruments of repression.

Their philosophy is simple: without law, there is no survival. They see mercy as weakness, and dissent as a threat greater than the frost itself. This conviction leads them to carry out harsh punishments for theft or disobedience and many citizens view this as brutal but necessary. For the Lawkeepers, justice is not about fairness, but about survival through unity and control.

docs.title: Voting
docs.text:
The colony holds elections in certain intervals. During those voting cycles the governing faction is determined. Every inhabitant of the colony is capable to vote for either lawkeepers or faithkeepers during a voting cycle.

In order to cast a vote the voting menu (assign hotkey in the controls menu) must be used. Each player who is online at the time of voting may cast one vote for either faction. Chose wisely - the vote can not be changed after it has been cast! During each voting cycle a different faction my be chosen.

After the voting cycle ended the controling power over the colony is transfered to the new governing faction. The members of the new coverning faction is granted the power to perform all the special actions like building, upgrades and more.

docs.title: Amputation
docs.text:
If frostbite progression has gone to far of the rails medicine wont save you anymore. The day to day struggle with frostbite will eventually be so unbearable that living with it is not an option anymore.

The only thing thats left to save the player will be an amputation. Amputation can be performed on the left and right foot depending on which one being affected.

In order for a player to undergo surgery the performing player needs the appropriate skill and a bone saw. The receiving player is advised to be put under heavy pain medicine or either be in a good and healthy state besides having frostbite.

After receiving the amputation a new slot in the inventory of the player will be unlocked . This slot will enable the player to put on foot/leg prosthetics helping to midigate the lost foot.

Prosthetics are available for left and right foot and can be crafted using the workbench if according skill has been unlocked.

docs.title: Body Hygiene
docs.text:
Living around the generater is anything else but a clean living space. A running generator constantly pushes ash into the air. Over time the player will get dirty which will be indicated visually on the players face and hands.

Being dirty makes you vulnarable against other infections and diseases. Make sure to wash yourself using a bottle of water. In order to wash yourself put the bottle in your hands and take off all clothing. A action to wash yourself will appear. Washing will drain your heatbuffer.

docs.title: Food Diet
docs.text:
The food diet is a (to the player) hidden stat. It is influenced by the food a player consumes. "Bad" food will decrease the state and "good" food will increase it. (Food can also be neutral having no impact on the stat).

If the stat gets to low the player will get sick. Make sure to balance the food consumes by the player.

docs.title: Frostbite
docs.text:
Frostbite is a negative progressive condition impacting the player either constantly or over time. Frostbite consists of 4 stages complementing each other in negative effects on the player.

If the player started to get frostbite there is no need to worry. As long as the progression is in stage 1 refilling the heat buffer and staying warm will be sufficient to treat the early stage.

Higher stages will need dedicated treatment while final stages can no longer be cured and amputation is the only option that is left.

docs.title: Heat Buffer
docs.text:
The vanilla heatbuffer/heatcomfort stat is replaced by a custom implementation. The stats represents the core state around the positive or negative temperature deficite.

The stat is represented by the following icon in the player stats hud:

As long as this stat is not empty environmental temperate has no impact on the player. Therefore it is crucial for the player to keep the stat at a reasonable level and always pay attention to it. Once the heat buffer emptied out completely the player will start to get frostbite

The stat drops whenever there is a negative temperature deficite. It raises when there is a positive temperature deficite.

The speeed at which the heat buffer refills or empties out generally depends on the delta between the environmental temperature and the temperature deficite. The loss of heat buffer can be slowed down by using clothing with good insulation values. A cold protection metere is placed in the bottom left corner of the inventory: Note: A full protection bar does not mean the player wont suffer loss of heat buffer it only indicates that the maximum protection level has been achieved

If the heatbuffer emptied out and the protection against the cold is not high enough the player may slowely freeze to death. Freezing to death is indicated by the following status badge indicator: Freezing to death can only be countered by refilling the heatbuffer stat.

docs.title: Heat Level
docs.text:
The heat level indicates the positive or negative temperature delta based on the overall temperature. It is indicated by a status badge indicator () on the player status hud the same way as vanilla status indicators are shown.

The added or substracted heat level is shown as an additional bage indicator value on the status badge.

Each positive level provides enough to heat to counter -10°C of environmental temperatue. The heatlevel directly impacts the heat buffer stat

Bonus Tipp: The environmental temperature and how it will change over time can be observed using the beacon

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Resources are items that can be stored in the resource depot. They can be used for crafting, building, or cooking. Once they are stored in the resource depot player receives reward in form of heat stamps.. Only the governing faction is allowed to withdraw resources from resource depot.

Resources are divided into types that are designated by icons

  • Coal
  • Raw Wood
  • Processed Wood
  • Raw Metal
  • Processed Metal
  • Raw Meat
  • Raw Vegetables
  • Raw Biomass
  • Fabric
  • Leather
  • Pelt
  • Steam Core

The following list shows buildings and what resource this building can produce

  • Coal Mine
  • Charcoal Kiln — converts 1 Raw Wood into 4 Coal per minute.
  • Wall Drill
  • Sawmill
  • Steelworks
  • Hothouse

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
There are 3 types of skills

  • Food & Health
  • Technology
  • Hunting & Exploration

In order to unlock skills you need skill points. Each of the skill types has different skill points indicated by icons in the skill menu. Menu can be by default opened with K key (it can be changed in settings). Skill points are acquired by doing things that are connected to said skill trees. For example healing people gives experience to the Food & Health skill tree, hunting and venturing out into the wilderness give experience to Hunting & Exploration etc. Keep in mind that there is many more ways to get experience other than listed examples.

There are 5 tiers of skills in each of the skill trees. You need at least half of the skills in previous tier to unlock the next tier. To see description of the skill you need to click on a skill that you can learn. This description also shows how many skill points certain skill needs and button that allows you to unlock this particular skill.

Skills by default unlock new abilities, recipes or improve actions such as speed of the action, yield of resources etc.

docs.title: Food & Health
docs.text: This skill tree helps with sustaining life in and outside of the colony. Anything that is connected with horticulture, cooking or healthcare can be found in this tree. Doing such things will provide you with experience for this skill tree.

docs.title: Hunting & Exploration
docs.text: This skill tree is for people who are ready to venture out. Anything that is connected with hunting, exploring or surviving outside of the colony can be found in this tree. Doing such things will provide you with experience for this skill tree.

docs.title: Technology
docs.text: This skill tree helps with advancement of the colony. Anything that is connected with technology, labor or general crafting can be found in this tree. Doing such things will provide you with experience for this skill tree.
